caption: Figure 1: Observed one-hour melEDI in the primary frames. Panel A summarizes positive observations using the 10th–90th percentile line, 25th–75th percentile thick line, median point, and open 99th-percentile point on a true symlog axis. Panel B shows the share of exact-zero hours retained in the models.
alt: Two-panel distribution display for near-eye and chest one-hour melEDI. Positive values span a broad right-skewed range on an axis that is linear from zero to one lux and logarithmic above one lux. The adjacent panel shows that exact zeros comprise about 28 to 29 percent of fitted hours.

caption: Figure 2: Observed participant support for each joint day-type and activity category by study site and placement. Point size represents supported hours; crosses mark cells without observations and open circles mark observed cells with fewer than four participants or eight participant-days. Colours identify sites only.
alt: Two-panel dot matrix of four day-type and activity combinations across nine near-eye and eight chest sites: Borås (SE), Delft (NL), Dortmund (DE), Tübingen (DE), Munich (DE), Madrid (ES), Izmir (TR), San José (CR), and Kumasi (GH). Every primary near-eye site has observations in all four combinations, though some free-day sedentary cells are sparse. Chest data are absent for Tübingen (DE). Point sizes show supported hours, shapes distinguish support categories, and colours identify sites.

caption: Figure 3: Supported participant-hours across local clock time for the four joint day-type and activity categories. Colour and line type jointly identify category; panels separate near-eye and chest. The display describes fitted-row support rather than an exposure effect.
alt: Two-panel line chart of supported participant-hours at each local clock hour. Work-day Active hours are most numerous, followed by Free-day Active hours; Sedentary categories have fewer observations. Support remains present across all 24 clock hours at both placements.
